messages:
anna_ng: Heads up — ran a multi-model co-residency perf pass on staging. hitting intermittent OOMs when two mid-size models + large KV cache are packed on a single A100. profile attached below (quick summary).

kevin_w: Can you paste the profiler highlights? is it fragmentation or a single hot allocation? :thinking:

anna_ng: Mostly fragmentation + workspace spikes. Kernel selection changed for forward attention (switch to fused matmul+softmax kernel) and that kernel grabs a larger workspace on some sequence lengths. We saw transient peaks: ~48GB used -> then kernels request an extra 8-12GB workspace leading to OOM.

marta_r: that sounds like cudnn/cublas workspace growth. Did you see spikes tied to specific sequence-length distributions?

anna_ng: yes — bursts align with batched requests where sequence length variance is high. Batching heuristic currently packs by arrival and just concatenates sequences; it doesn't try to homogenize seq-len. So a single long sequence in the batch forces kernel to pick a bigger workspace for the whole batch.

samir_k: ugh. we knew the packing policy was naive. Two quick levers: (1) batching heuristic: prioritize grouping similar seq-len or cap max padding per batch, (2) limit per-kernel workspace via runner config so it falls back to a smaller kernel variant.

jessica_t: On the KV side, are we pinning per-model caches in GPU memory? If both models keep full KV caches for long-running chats, that'll saturate VRAM fast.

anna_ng: current behavior: KV caches are local to session and live in GPU until session idle timeout (default 30m). We don't auto-evict or compress across co-resident models. Seen instances where two streams keep 12GB+ each.

kevin_w: we should consider per-model soft quotas + LRU eviction across sessions. Also buffer reuse across models — reuse same allocator arenas for ephemeral tensors rather than separate pools per model.

marta_r: agree. allocator tuning that helped previously: reduce max arena size from 80%->65% of GPU memory to leave headroom for workspace spikes, enable smaller bin sizes, and activate cross-context buffer reuse. That reduced fragmentation in bench runs.

samir_k: notes from profiling run (raw):
```
- peak resident: 48.1 GB
- sudden kernel workspace bump: +11.3 GB at t=00:02:14 (attention kernel v2-fused)
- kv total: 25.4 GB (modelA: 12.8, modelB: 12.6)
- free segments fragmented: 1.2k small blocks (<= 256KB)
- allocator stalls: several realloc attempts in critical path
```

anna_ng: proposal:
- Batching: introduce a "seq-homogenize" option in packer to avoid mixing long+short in single batch, and cap pad inflation to 20%.
- Kernel selection: expose workspace cap per model route; if kernel workspace > cap, fallback to alternate kernel (slower but bounded).
- KV policy: per-model soft quota + LRU eviction to host pinned memory when over threshold. Avoid copying to host unless idle for >5m.
- Allocator: tune arena max to 65% and enable buffer reuse across models (global freelist). Also add a proactive defragment pass during low-load windows.

jessica_t: can you share a sample config for the residency+swap policy? I want to try in staging.

anna_ng: sample (pseudo) config: 
```json
{
  "vram_partitions": [
    {"model": "modelA", "min_mb": 10240, "soft_quota_mb": 12288},
    {"model": "modelB", "min_mb": 10240, "soft_quota_mb": 12288}
  ],
  "swap_policy": {
    "evict_to_host_after_idle_s": 300,
    "evict_when_used_percent": 0.85,
    "prefetch_on_request": true,
    "allow_shared_buffer_reuse": true
  },
  "kernel_workspace_cap_mb": 8192,
  "batching": {"seq_homogenize": true, "pad_limit_percent": 20}
}
```

kevin_w: nice. for swap-to-host path we should prefer pinned host pages and async memcpy to overlap swap with compute. Avoid blocking the main inference thread.

marta_r: any perf regression risks? falling back to non-fused kernels will increase latency tail. We need a cost model: if workspace cap forces a fallback, auto-reduce batch size to keep latency SLO instead of fallback kernel.

samir_k: +1. Also measure the end-to-end p99 impact in the eval harness. We want to trade small latency increase for no OOMs. In a lot of customer cases OOMs are worse.

allocator-bot: automated note: created ticket INF-4291 "co-residency allocator tuning + swap policy" and attached profiling snapshot.

jessica_t: I'll spin up a canary with that config and run the model pair under synthetic mixed seq-len traffic. Leaving some headroom on arenas and enabling seq_homogenize for 24h.

anna_ng: thanks — if canary looks good we can gate the change behind a rollout flag and add metrics: kernel_workspace_fallback_count, kv_evictions_to_host, allocator_fragmentation_ratio.

kevin_w: Also add a soft-deny route: if combined soft_quotas exceed physical memory, reject new model loads with a clear error explaining swap or request dedicated instance. Better than silent OOM.

marta_r: agree. action items:
- anna: push allocator config + kernel cap prototype (today)
- jessica: run canary (this afternoon)
- samir: add eviction instrumentation to KV layer (end of day)
- kevin: write fallback policy for packer (tomorrow)

anna_ng: will update the ticket with diffs. thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin_w: quick follow-up — if we implement global freelist, watch for cross-model safety with CUDA streams. Need to ensure buffers are idle / synchronized before reuse.

anna_ng: yep, plan is to tag buffers with last-used-stream and only recycle after stream-synchronize or fence completion.

samir_k: one more thought: for very hot small models, consider memory compaction by reloading weights in quantized format on demand. That could reduce the memory footprint and make co-residency denser.

jessica_t: noted. will test quantized weight swap as a later optimization.

anna_ng: end of thread — will paste canary results here once available.
